name: Leh (Ladakh)
tagline: High-desert monasteries and the roof of India
summary: Leh is the capital of Ladakh, a high-altitude desert of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, prayer flags and moonscape mountains at 3,500 m. Acclimatise slowly, then visit Thiksey and Hemis monasteries, drive over one of the world's highest roads to the Nubra Valley's dunes and Bactrian camels, and see the colour-shifting Pangong Lake.
seasonNote: June to September; road passes close in winter. Rest your first two days for the altitude.
arrival: Flights from Delhi take 1h20; road access from Manali or Srinagar in summer.
gettingAround: Hire a car with driver; Inner Line Permits are needed for Nubra and Pangong (arranged in Leh).
cashTip: UPI is everywhere but foreign cards may not link; carry rupees for small places and taxis. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants.
foodTip: Thukpa, momos, skyu (pasta stew), butter tea and apricots.
buyTip: Pashmina, thangka paintings and dried apricots.
